svg.title: Cost-of-Waiting Gate Before Committing to a Queue Position
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-05-cost-of-waiting-decision-tree; chapter number: 5; chart type: decision_tree; title: Cost-of-Waiting Gate Before Committing to a Queue Position; subtitle: The plug, not the panel or the chip, sets the clock; caption: Median 2025 builds waited 61 months from request to commercial operation, versus 36 months in 2015 and 22 months in 2008 (THE PHYSICAL LAYER).; assumptions note: Gate order is a screening sequence assembled from practitioner operator gates. Per-kW benchmarks, attrition shares and the $598M upgrade bill are attributed practitioner claims drawn from Berkeley Lab and PJM study figures they cited.; note: Attributed to Wattlore (CDd-hsI3tKQ), The Pharos Project (Br7K7fGD4uk), US Energy Weekly (DzkVggOvJGs) and learnBESS (m0yVO4ZOmdc).; nodes: gate: G1; question: Divided by project kW, is the network upgrade estimate near the roughly $84/kW completed projects paid rather than the roughly $600/kW of projects that quit?; pass next: G2; fail action: Re-price or exit; one 51 MW New Jersey solar farm drew a $598M bill, more than $11,000 per kW (Wattlore).; gate: G2; question: Are the projects ahead of you solid, with attrition priced in and the queue number quoted with its date?; pass next: G3; fail action: Haircut the headline queue; only about 13% of 2000-2020 requested capacity came online and 75% withdrew (The Pharos Project).; gate: G3; question: On an ERCOT connect-and-manage site, is curtailment modeled for when the wires are full?; pass next: G4; fail action: Model curtailment before committing, because it hits revenue directly (US Energy Weekly).; gate: G4; question: Can arbitrage, balancing and capacity be stacked through one route-to-market provider?; pass next: Advance to the interconnection request; fail action: Rework the revenue case; a single stream rarely justifies the investment (learnBESS).

rect.title: gate: G1; question: Divided by project kW, is the network upgrade estimate near the roughly $84/kW completed projects paid rather than the roughly $600/kW of projects that quit?; pass next: G2; fail action: Re-price or exit; one 51 MW New Jersey solar farm drew a $598M bill, more than $11,000 per kW (Wattlore).

gate: G2; question: Are the projects ahead of you solid, with attrition priced in and the queue number quoted with its date?; pass next: G3; fail action: Haircut the headline queue; only about 13% of 2000-2020 requested capacity came online and 75% withdrew (The Pharos Project).

gate: G3; question: On an ERCOT connect-and-manage site, is curtailment modeled for when the wires are full?; pass next: G4; fail action: Model curtailment before committing, because it hits revenue directly (US Energy Weekly).

gate: G4; question: Can arbitrage, balancing and capacity be stacked through one route-to-market provider?; pass next: Advance to the interconnection request; fail action: Rework the revenue case; a single stream rarely justifies the investment (learnBESS).

text.title: Assumptions: Gate order is a screening sequence assembled from practitioner operator gates. Per-kW benchmarks, attrition shares and the $598M upgrade bill are attributed practitioner claims drawn from Berkeley Lab and PJM study figures they cited.
